# hitron

> Reverse-engineered clients, a complete OpenAPI 3.0 description, and one
> exporter for Hitron CODA6X (CODA-60 class), CODA-57, and HT-EM5 gateways.
> The exporter emits Prometheus text, Influx line protocol (Telegraf),
> OTLP/HTTP JSON (OpenTelemetry), and plain JSON from a single normalized
> metric vocabulary.

Everything here is derived from a signed CODA-60 firmware image and live
responses, not from vendor documentation. Field names and casing are the
firmware's own, including typos such as `Raidos_List`.

## Start here

- [Getting started, end to end](https://github.com/Netquor/hitron/blob/main/docs/GETTING-STARTED.md): install, verify, export, scrape, alert, troubleshoot.
- [Grafana tutorial](https://github.com/Netquor/hitron/blob/main/docs/GRAFANA.md): dashboards, panels, alerts, Loki.
- [Reverse-engineering knowledge base](https://github.com/Netquor/hitron/blob/main/docs/KB.md): auth model, shell sinks, firmware quirks.
- [Static site](https://hitron.netquor.dev/): API console, live charts, logs.
- [Run the site and gateway proxy locally](https://github.com/Netquor/hitron/blob/main/docs/LOCAL-PROXY.md): one-line installer, pipx/uv alternatives, troubleshooting.
- Installer script: https://hitron.netquor.dev/install.sh (`curl -fsSL ... | bash`); Windows: https://hitron.netquor.dev/install.ps1.
- Standalone Go client and live terminal dashboard (`hitron-cli monitor`), no runtime: https://github.com/Netquor/hitron/tree/main/cli (releases at /releases). Showcase and getting started: https://hitron.netquor.dev/#cli
- [Source](https://github.com/Netquor/hitron)

## API specifications

- CODA6X console API (CODA-60 class), full: `specs/openapi-coda60.yaml`.
  116 paths, 171 operations, envelope `{errCode, errMsg}`, `errCode == "000"`
  means success. Request bodies are a form field `model` holding JSON;
  `_method` tunnels PUT/DELETE/PATCH through POST.
- HT-EM5 MoCA bridge: `specs/openapi-ht-em5.yaml`.
- CODA-57 legacy `.asp` API: `specs/openapi-coda57-legacy.yaml`.
- Rendered JSON for tooling: `site/openapi.json`.

Base URLs: `http://192.168.100.1` (factory LAN), or the address your ISP build
uses. Auth in the analyzed build is disabled for reads and for the two FEC
counter clears; the other writes use session cookies or a vendor `Ht-App-Auth`
header.

## Commands

    pip install -e ".[dev]"

    hitron coda60 192.168.100.1            # read everything, print JSON
    hitron coda57 192.168.100.2 --spec-check
    hitron ht-em5 192.168.0.212

    hitron-cli 192.168.100.1               # Go binary: live TUI
    hitron-cli monitor                     # TUI views: 1 stats, 2 spectrum, 3 constellation, z FEC reset
    hitron-cli fec-reset --json            # clear 3.0 + OFDM FEC counters, no login
    hitron-cli stats --once --json         # one report, machine-readable
    hitron-cli reboot --confirm -u admin -p admin

    hitron-exporter --coda60 192.168.100.1 --ht-em5 192.168.0.212
    hitron-exporter --coda60 edge=192.168.100.1 --once --format telegraf
    hitron-exporter --coda60 192.168.100.1 --once --format otlp
    hitron-exporter --coda60 192.168.100.1 --otlp-endpoint http://collector:4318/v1/metrics

    hitron grafana --dir deploy/grafana   # regenerate dashboards + provisioning
    hitron site --device 192.168.100.1    # static docs + gateway proxy on :8000

Exporter endpoints: `/metrics`, `/healthz`, `/api/v1/samples`, `/api/v1/logs`.

## Metric vocabulary

Prefix `modem_` for CODA6X and CODA-57; `hitron_` for HT-EM5 and self-metrics.
Counters end in `_total`. Labels are bounded identifiers, never free text.

- `modem_downstream_channel_power_dbmv{source,channel_id,port_id}`
- `modem_downstream_channel_snr_db{source,channel_id}`
- `modem_downstream_channel_{octets,corrected,uncorrectable}_total`
- `modem_upstream_channel_power_dbmv{source,channel_id}`
- `modem_downstream_ofdm_channel_{plc_power_dbmv,snr_db,frequency_hz}`
- `modem_downstream_ofdm_channel_{plc,ncp,mdc1}_locked`
- `modem_upstream_ofdm_channel_{power_dbmv,power_1_6_dbmv,bandwidth_mhz,operating}`
- `modem_power_in_spec{direction}` (CODA-57, envelope configurable)
- `modem_wifi_client_count{band}`, `modem_wifi_client_rssi_dbm`
- `modem_host_count`, `modem_host_info`, `modem_ethernet_port_link_up`
- `modem_moca_link_up`, `hitron_moca_phy_rate_mbps{node_id,peer_node_id}`
- `hitron_exporter_up{source,kind}`, `hitron_exporter_scrape_error_info`

## Dashboards and deployment

- `dashboards/hitron-coda6x.json`, `dashboards/hitron-ht-em5.json` (importable)
- `deploy/compose.yaml` (exporter + Prometheus + Grafana + Loki + Promtail)
- `deploy/prometheus/prometheus.yml`, `deploy/telegraf/telegraf.conf`,
  `deploy/otel/collector.yaml`, `deploy/grafana/prometheus/rules/hitron.rules.yml`

## Safety

`POST /1/Device/CM/Reboot` reads three flags before choosing a branch, so every
body must carry all of them: `{"reboot":0,"factoryReset":0,"restoreReset":1}` is
the only combination measured to reboot (the connection drops with no reply, the
unit is back about two minutes later). `{"reboot":1}` answers `errCode 000` and
does nothing; a partial body is a PHP 8 fatal. The Python CLI guards these
behind `--yes-really-do-this`, the Go CLI behind `--confirm`.
`PUT /1/Device/CM/DsInfo` and `PUT /1/Device/CM/DsOfdm`
clear the 3.0 and OFDM FEC counters with no body and no session; the TUI binds
both to `z`, and `hitron-cli fec-reset` runs them headlessly; the OFDM stop is
unreliable on this build.
`/1/Device/Upload`,
`/1/Device/AdminRemoteManagement/Restore`, and credential routes also mutate
the device. The exporter never calls any of them.
